expectedTruths: The (N-1)-divisor sample covariance of data.csv equals the population model-implied covariance in population.json (impliedCovariance) and the sample means equal the population means, to ~1e-12.

A consistent common-factor estimator (PLSc; ML CB-SEM) returns, to solver tolerance: paths PEOU->PU = 0.60, PEOU->BI = 0.20, PU->BI = 0.50; indirect PEOU->BI = 0.30; total PEOU->BI = 0.50; standardised loadings peou1..4 = .80,.78,.76,.74, pu1..4 = .85,.82,.80,.78, bi1..3 = .88,.85,.82; R^2(PU) = 0.36, R^2(BI) = 0.410000.

ML chi-square = 0 (to solver tolerance) with df = 41: 66 covariance moments minus 25 free parameters (8 free loadings + 11 residual variances + 1 exogenous latent variance + 2 disturbance variances + 3 paths under marker identification). With a mean structure, 11 means and 11 intercepts are added and df stays 41.

Unstandardised ML variances are (N-1)/N = 499/500 times the population values when the estimator uses the N-divisor sample covariance (lavaan default likelihood='normal'); standardised estimates are unaffected.

Classic PLS-SEM (Mode A, no consistency correction) converges to the population limit in population.json derivedTruths.classicPlsPopulationLimit: PEOU->PU = 0.522341, PEOU->BI = 0.203603, PU->BI = 0.443823, indirect = 0.231827, total = 0.435430. PEOU->PU, PU->BI, the indirect and the total effect are ATTENUATED relative to the common-factor values; the direct PEOU->BI path is NOT attenuated (it is slightly larger than 0.20), because multiple-regression coefficients on attenuated correlations need not all shrink.
